sipser.title: Introduction to the Theory of Computation

hmu.title: Introduction to Automata Theory, Languages, and Computation
hmu.authors: John E. Hopcroft, Rajeev Motwani and Jeffrey D. Ullman

words-and-languages.why: The course book's first reference; defines alphabets, strings and languages the same way.

regular-expressions.why: Regular expressions and their equivalence with finite automata, used throughout the course book.

deterministic-finite-automata.why: The 5-tuple definition and the automaton examples the course book reuses.

deterministic-finite-automata.read: Chapter 4: Properties of Regular Languages (equivalence and minimization of automata)
deterministic-finite-automata.why: The table-filling method for minimising a DFA.

nondeterministic-finite-automata.why: NFAs, ε-transitions and the subset construction, with the NFA N1 the course book uses.

properties-of-regular-languages.why: The pumping lemma and proofs that languages are not regular.

context-free-grammars.why: CFGs, derivations, ambiguity and Chomsky normal form.

pushdown-automata.why: PDAs and their equivalence with context-free grammars.
